coverage.description: Complete 2020 Census ZCTA 60601; all polygon components and holes retained.

355 supported mapped building/park ways inside the exact boundary. OpenStreetMap is a contributed map, not an exhaustive inventory. Unmapped buildings and roads remain unknown. 12 complex relation features were not imported; multipolygon building/park support is still required for a complete inventory. 435 fetched footprints outside or crossing the exact ZCTA boundary were excluded; partial buildings are not modeled.
2425 mapped street/path pieces clipped to the exact ZCTA; lane/speed gaps use labeled estimates.

Illustrative OSM inference v1.1: mapped use tags where present; otherwise footprints below 200 m² are assumed residential and larger footprints office. Missing height uses levels × 3.5 m; missing floors use mapped height or use/footprint heuristics (1–5 floors). Mapped flats are used when present; otherwise one home per assumed house or 100 m² gross floor area per apartment. Jobs use gross floor area × illustrative jobs per 1,000 ft² (office4, retail/school2, industrial1.5, warehouse0.5, healthcare/civic3). Parking structures use30 m² per space. These are unvalidated capacity estimates, not observed population/employment/parking. Geometry completeness varies; review all assumptions.
Authoritative parcel and zoning data are not included.
No calibrated traffic counts, intersection LOS, regional routing, or GTFS transit is included.
No LODES employment, flood/hazard, or premium licensed data are included.
2020–2024 ACS five-year estimates for ZCTA 60601, with 90% margins. Whole study geography.

method.description: Sum B15003 cells 022, 023, 024, 025 and divide by total cell 001. These approximate margins omit component covariance and can differ from published Data Profile margins.
method.formula: P = sum(component estimates) / total; MOE = 100 / total × √(sum(component MOE²) − P² × total MOE²). Use + if the radicand is negative.

notes: Five-year survey estimates describe 2020–2024, not a current-year count or forecast.
A ZCTA is a statistical approximation of a postal ZIP. Published whole-area counts are not scaled to mapped buildings.
Population, household, housing-unit, and median-income estimates and margins come directly from Detailed Tables.
Poverty and bachelor’s-or-higher percentages are derived from published counts. Their 90% margins are approximate, following Census handbook chapter 8; component covariance is unavailable.
A missing estimate or margin remains unavailable. Open-ended medians are not treated as exact values.
